doc.title: Steve Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 15, 2017

title: Tonight's gig and the way of life of jazz
summary: Talk of the evening's pick-up gig, Mike Dubaniewicz and Kris Jensen, and why he would not trade being a jazz musician.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well you speak well of the music, and I like the idea of your students having a teacher who has the bandstand experience as well as the academic background. So I’m going to wish you well on your gig tonight, with a semi-pick-up situation.
I hope they leave some space for you.

Oh yeah. I’m sure they will. Mike Dubaniewicz is a really cool cat. He played with Maynard and played with my good buddy Kris Jensen, who I grew up with in Binghamton, a great tenor player, not as well known as he should be in the jazz world, © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

but anybody who knows him knows he can really play. So they played with Maynard together. Oh I could go on and on. There’s a lot of great musicians who don’t — as you know — who really don’t get their due or appreciated enough. But you can’t do it for that. It’s a way of life. And you certainly can’t do it to get rich. But you do it because you love it and I wouldn’t trade it for the world, being a jazz musician. I wouldn’t trade it for the world.
